summary: Frontend-only iteration 17 retest passed all requested fixes on the public URL. LOCUS and HERACLES used distinct namespaced drag keys without cross-module inheritance; both PANTHEON secondary headings dragged their cards; ORACLE and ARGUS grip positions persisted after close/reopen; and the localhost WebSocket loop produced exactly 5 failures at 0.4s, 1.8s, 3.8s, 7.9s, and 15.9s, with no later failures during the 65+ second five-module traversal.
critical_code_review_comments: Non-blocking cleanup: useDraggableCards.js line 82 retains an unused eslint-disable directive; targeted ESLint reports one warning and no errors.
seed_data_creation: No backend data created. Browser-local drag keys were cleared, then isolated LOCUS, HERACLES, PANTHEON, ORACLE, and ARGUS position keys were created in the test context.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All three iteration 16 defects are verified fixed. In the complete run, LOCUS saved {x:42,y:26}, HERACLES first opened with an empty transform and saved {x:31,y:19}, and LOCUS restored its original transform. PANTHEON's TABLEAU DE CONNECTIVITÉ and HISTORIQUE DES CONNEXIONS headings both had cursor:grab and moved their respective cards. ORACLE data should be allowed to settle before dragging because its drag hook rebinds when overview data arrives.
rca_of_the_issue: The implemented fixes address the prior causes: storage keys now include the root panel namespace; querySelectorAll wires every matching heading; and the non-localhost reconnect guard stops after the initial connection plus four retries. Observed WebSocket failures followed exponential backoff and ceased after 15.9 seconds. No page errors or visible DOM errors occurred.
